name: Sriharikota SLP
tagline: India's heavy-lift pad — GSLV Mk III / LVM3 to Chandrayaan-3, Mangalyaan, and the upcoming Gaganyaan crew programme
description: Sriharikota Island on India's east coast, 13.7°N — closer to the equator than Cape Canaveral, with the Bay of Bengal corridor empty downrange. The Second Launch Pad (SLP) handles ISRO's heavy-lift programme: PSLV manifests, LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III), Chandrayaan-1 (October 2008, lunar orbiter/impactor), Chandrayaan-2 (July 2019, lost on landing), Chandrayaan-3 (July 2023, successful soft landing near the south pole), and the planned Gaganyaan crewed missions. The First Launch Pad next door handles smaller PSLV / SSLV manifests and hosted the Mangalyaan Mars launch (November 2013).
best_known_for: India's heavy-lift pad — GSLV Mk III / LVM3 to Chandrayaan-3, Mangalyaan, and the upcoming Gaganyaan crew programme
